ci_regression_followup.launcher_cause: The first readiness marker preceded PID/status/gateway output. Sending a signal immediately after that first line could exit the fake child before the remaining records. The reader now receives all four complete records before signaling; channel waits and captured output are bounded.
ci_regression_followup.secret_input_cause: Restoring canonical mode and echo without first discarding unread hidden bytes can reprocess retained input. The direct queued-input regression reproduces retained secret bytes before the fix. The final implementation uses TCIFLUSH then TCSANOW, including Ctrl-Z suspension; it discards input queued when the flush runs, with no atomicity claim across the syscalls and no protection claim for subsequent typing.
ci_regression_followup.node_probe_scope: Separate stopped-child SIGINT/SIGTERM probe on macOS: 16 native and 16 frozen Node22.14 trials showed no echo. This probe did not reproduce the Linux CI scheduling trigger and is not presented as proof that the trigger is resolved.
preserved_assertions: Terminal restoration and no synthetic secret echo
Ordered two-prompt setup, blank key rejection and Ctrl-C
Exactly one forwarded signal and reaped fake Claude child

terminal_restoration_correction.implementation: A shared helper issues tcflush(TCIFLUSH), then tcsetattr(TCSANOW) even when the flush fails. Restoration errors take precedence, no EINTR retry loop is used, and the successful-read path returns an error if either operation fails. Drop remains best effort and restores saved descriptor flags. Ctrl-Z invokes the same helper before suspension.
terminal_restoration_correction.discard_boundary: Only bytes already in the unread kernel input queue when TCIFLUSH runs are discarded. The two syscalls are not atomic; bytes arriving after the flush, including typing after cancellation, are outside this boundary. Completed or cancelled editors discard their owned buffered input; Ctrl-Z retains its already-read editor state.
terminal_restoration_correction.regression: A bounded child process stops PTY output using TCOOFF and attempts a nonblocking output write. Drop and explicit restoration must return before any master read or TCOON, and restored terminal attributes and descriptor flags must match. macOS queues 33 output bytes in this fixture; Linux PTYs may return EAGAIN immediately. A five-second deadline kills and reaps a blocked child so an output-draining regression cannot hang the test runner.
terminal_restoration_correction.fixture_failure_explanation: The first regression compared raw F_GETFL bits with an OFlag-truncated original. Writing synthetic stopped output introduced an unrepresented 0x10000 flag on this macOS host. The final assertion compares the same OFlag set on both sides, including O_NONBLOCK; full terminal attributes remain checked.
limits: Executed on macOS arm64; fresh Linux CI and a newly installed artifact remain separate qualification.
Actual Ctrl-Z stop/resume with a controlling terminal is not covered; retaining O_NONBLOCK during suspension is pre-existing and unchanged.
This correction removes the terminal-attribute output-drain wait. Existing synchronous prompt/newline writes are unchanged and are not qualified against stalled terminal output.
Flush and restoration errors are not retried indefinitely; Drop cannot report errors. No atomicity or later-typing protection is claimed.
